precise_theorem: Thm 1 (p.2): optimal simple counterfeiting attack on Wiesner's n-qubit scheme succeeds with probability exactly (3/4)^n. Thm 2 (p.3) / Lemma 5 (p.14): classical-verification variant, optimal simple counterfeiting attack (two independent challenges answered from one ticket) succeeds with probability exactly (3/4+sqrt(2)/8)^n. Sec 3.5 eq.(4): binomial-tail bound for a joint-threshold variant (see THEOREM_REGISTRY_SEED T-MVW12-SEC35).
input_model: Bank prepares n qubits, each uniformly from {|0>,|1>,|+>,|->}; secret key k kept by bank; unique serial number; ideal noiseless states.
verifier_model: W1: bank applies projective measurement {Pi=|psi_k><psi_k|, 1-Pi} on each returned note (exact, accept-all-qubits). W1_CV: bank sends uniformly random challenge c in {0,1}^n, user measures qubit i in Z if c_i=0 or X if c_i=1; bank accepts iff all outcomes in matching-basis positions are correct; verification destroys the ticket.
adversary_capabilities: Arbitrary CPTP channel from one note register X to two registers (Y,Z) (W1), or arbitrary POVM depending on both challenges (c1,c2) (W1_CV). NO additional access to the bank's verifier (no adaptive verification queries); single note; independent verification of both outputs.
tested_parameters: Analytic; n arbitrary. n=1 SDP optimum 3/4 with explicit primal (Kraus A0,A1 p.8) and dual Y=(3/8)I. Also: 6-state/SIC ensembles -> (2/3)^n; d-dim 3-design -> 2/(d+1); qudit classical verification -> (3/4+1/(4 sqrt d))^n.
proof_dependencies: SDP duality (Slater, Thm 3); Choi-Jamiolkowski; product property of SDPs with PSD objective (Mittal-Szegedy) for n-fold repetition (Sec 3.4).
code: none released (paper mentions CVX used during research; not published)
license: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence 1.0 (paper text). No code.
limitations: Only 'simple counterfeiting' (1 note -> 2 notes, no verifier interaction). Paper explicitly notes other attacks exist (e.g. 2^-n Bell-state attack with verifier interaction; Lutomirski O(n) attack when post-verification qubits are returned). Ideal states/verifier; no loss/noise in Thm 1/2.
what_QMint_adds: Nothing new theoretically. QMint may reproduce Thm 1 (n=1 SDP + analytic n) as an L1 reproduction and use it as a golden test for game W1 only.
access_status: FULL_TEXT_READ (abs page + arXiv PDF v1, 18 pp)
